summary: Repeated request timeouts during ultra-long max_tokens calls due to scheduler preemption
description: Issue summary: Customer reports repeated 504/timeout responses when making single-shot generation calls with extremely large max_tokens (100k-200k) and multi-turn priming (~120k tokens). Impact: Customer workloads (document synthesis pipeline) are failing intermittently; several runs aborted mid-generation causing downstream job failures and duplicate costs. Environment: prod us-west, hosted API, requests using streaming enabled=true and batching policy default. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send POST /v1/generate with model=redwood-v1-large, prompt ~120k tokens, max_tokens=150000, streaming=true. 2) Observe first ~30-120 seconds of token emission, then a pause followed by a 504 or connection reset. 3) Retrying immediately sometimes succeeds if run is routed to a different worker. Logs and artifacts: customer provided request_id headers (x-rwinf-request: rw-req-73a9), and a tcpdump of the client connection. Support captured server-side trace: scheduler assigned to worker-23 -> preempted for priority rollback -> worker swap with kernel context load -> finalizer deadline expired -> 504. See attached trace snippets (customer and internal).
comments: 2026-03-12 09:14 - Jamal Rivera: Customer opened after 6 consecutive failures. They observe partial streams (first ~500-2000 tokens) then silence until client times out.
2026-03-12 10:02 - Support (Aisha): Requested request_id and full tooling trace; asked customer to temporarily set max_tokens to 50k as a workaround while we investigate.
2026-03-12 13:20 - Customer (Reverie): Tried 50k and saw successful runs but results are truncated for their use-case. Queried whether dedicated routing helps.

2026-03-13 08:45 - SRE (Diego): Reproduced internal repro on staging by scheduling a job with a 130k token priming prompt and max_tokens=120k. Observed worker preemption spikes and kernel swap during KV restore.
2026-03-14 11:00 - Aisha: Engaged runtime team; scheduled hotfix candidate to avoid preemption for long-running generation tasks and to increase finalizer deadline for preemption paths.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Long-running generation with very large KV and checkpoint state makes workers vulnerable to scheduler-driven preemption (to satisfy higher-priority reserved bursts). When preemption occurs mid-generation we observe heavy kernel/state swap activity (KV restore and quantized weights reload) which adds tens of seconds; finalizer TTL currently expires and API returns 504. Evidence: server traces show 'preempt_start' spikes correlated with increased cluster autoscale events at 09:10-09:20 UTC. Worker-23 logs: repeated 'evicting-older-job' events and subsequent 'load-kv-from-s3' operations. Repro on staging shows identical timeline: emission stalls, worker reassignment, then 504 after finalizer wdog. Additional finding: when batching=false and client uses streaming keepalive pings, some runs avoid early 504s but still show extended tail latency. Related config: batch window default and preemption policy 'aggressive' for user pool.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigations applied 2026-03-14: 1) Changed scheduler policy for self_serve pool in us-west to 'minimize-preempt' for requests with header x-rwinf-long-context=true (customer instructed to set this header). 2) Increased finalizer deadline for preemption path from 60s to 180s as a stopgap. 3) Recommended customer workaround: set max_tokens <= 60k or enable request chunking (submit shorter continuation calls) and disable batching for these endpoints. Current status: mitigations reduced 504 rate from ~70% to ~8% for affected customers; longer term fix in progress.
next_steps: - Runtime team to implement kernel/context hot-swap optimization (avoid full KV reload on preemption) — tracked in ENG-rt-993 (ETA 2 weeks). - Scheduler team to add long-context detection built-in (no header required) and a safer default for self_serve pools (ETA 1 week). - Product to document best-practices (chunking guidance) in public KB. - Follow-up with Reverie to offer Dedicated routing evaluation if SLA/throughput needs justify it.
postmortem_followup_items: SCHED-271: long-context detection and preemption policy change (1w)
DOC-188: KB article on chunking and max_tokens guidance
